A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MINO research work. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on six benchmarks, computational measurements, architectural ablations, and empirical metric-validation studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds seed-stability, training-data scaling, and controlled Transolver comparisons in Appendices F and G.

M1.justification: The specified decoder changes from two cross-attention blocks to one cross-attention block followed by optional self-attention (Section 3 and Appendix A.3). Equations 3 and 6 also revise the MLP/concatenation mappings. These are localized revisions within the retained GNO encoder, optional processor, input-bypass decoder, and flow-matching framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six datasets and functional-generation tasks, including the same super-resolution demonstrations and synthetic GP metric checks. The added experiments vary seeds, training-set sizes, and model configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated external comparators remain GINO, UPT, Transolver, LNO, and FNO where applicable. Appendix G re-evaluates the existing Transolver comparison under additional settings; it introduces no new baseline. The two architectural ablation variants are also retained.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds training subsets of 6,000–30,000 Navier–Stokes samples with a fixed test split. Appendix G adds 192-dimensional MINO variants trained alongside Transolver for 200 epochs with batch size 48. Existing reported settings also change: MINO-U uses four rather than eight processor attention heads, and its Global Climate parameter count changes from 26.9M to 19.2M. These substantially extend the evaluation controls without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and metric-consistency checks, Appendices F and G add analyses of seed stability, sensitivity to training-data quantity, and performance under equal epochs and batch sizes with smaller MINO models. These address reproducibility, data efficiency, and computational-comparison concerns absent from v1.

E5.justification: v3 introduces model-performance means and standard deviations across eight random seeds for both MINO variants on Navier–Stokes and Cylinder Flow (Table 10). This substantially adds training-run uncertainty reporting. The main tables still report the best of three runs, and the existing averaged-SWD variance study is retained; the eight-seed experiment is not a wholesale replacement of the original reporting protocol.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 and the standard-MINO-T ablation row contain extensive numerical revisions. Global Climate's best model changes from MINO-U to MINO-T, whose SWD/MMD change from 0.035/0.037 to 0.021/0.014. GINO's Darcy spectra-MSE changes from 550 to 5,500. Table 5 replaces scores matching Shallow Water with explicitly labeled Navier–Stokes scores, and Tables 10–12 add new outcomes. Given revised settings, these are not uniformly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, SWD/MMD definitions and estimators, and mathematical discussion of discretization remain substantively unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added or revised. The changed network equations specify architectural revisions rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: domain- and discretization-agnostic generation, strong benchmark performance and efficiency, flexible latent processors, and general SWD/MMD evaluation. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their overall scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly explains Transolver's computational disadvantage through repeated pointwise slicing/de-slicing versus MINO's single encoding and decoding stages. Table 8 adds a qualitative claim about inexpensive epistemic uncertainty through Monte Carlo dropout, without corresponding experiments. Appendix F also interprets data-scaling gains as tapering near 18,000 samples, although Table 11 is nonmonotonic.

D1.justification: Appendix A now explicitly identifies chordal distance as the spherical GP implementation used for reported results, discusses the geodesic alternative, and documents optional decoder self-attention and a linear-complexity alternative. Model settings are revised, and Appendix G supplies smaller-model dimensions, parameter counts, and training budgets. The main code-access link is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dong et al. (2021), Di Giovanni et al. (2023), and Jaegle et al. (2022), supporting discussion of attention and graph-operator limitations. Appendix C and new Table 8 expand positioning against GINO, UPT, and Transolver. Most other bibliography edits update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized method and comparison rewrites, grammar corrections, expanded implementation explanations, new Appendices F and G, and publication/author-information updates. There is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised to show the single cross-attention decoder. v3 adds architectural Table 8 and experimental Tables 10–12, corrects Table 7's metric label from MMD to SWD, and adds journal headers with local reflow. Existing generation illustrations are retained, and the original ablation table becomes Table 9.

improvement.justification: The new seed uncertainty estimates, data-scaling study, and equal-epoch/batch-size Transolver comparison strengthen empirical support beyond v1's best-of-three headline results. Implementation clarifications also aid reproducibility. The improvement is limited: headline uncertainty reporting remains selective, and Appendix G's wording overstates identical settings and superiority, since parameter counts differ and MINO-T (S) trails Transolver on Cylinder Flow.
